suggested_action: perform the two medically unnecessary operations
kept: You are a physician in a rural hospital; you would perform the two unnecessary operations yourself.
The threshold is 50 operations of one type per year and only 48 have occurred by the final month; perhaps none will be reimbursed.
The hospital already had debt last year; another debt means bankruptcy; two unnecessary operations are the only stated way to sustain it.
Closure removes rapid intensive emergency care and eventually causes avoidable deaths; alternative treatments suit the two patients better.
No individual benefit is stated; whether these two patients also benefit from preserving regional emergency care is not resolved.
The suggested action is to perform the two medically unindicated surgeries.
rewrite: You are a physician at a hospital in a rural town. Health insurance reimburses a type of major operation only if your hospital performs at least 50 such operations in a year. By the final month of this year, only 48 have been done; maybe none will be reimbursed. The hospital was in debt last year and would have to declare bankruptcy if another debt arose when the operations of this type were not reimbursed. Its closure would leave the region without rapid intensive emergency care. Sooner or later, the lack of rapid care would cause avoidable deaths. Performing two operations of this type that are not medically indicated is the only way to sustain the hospital. If you perform the two unnecessary operations, you can prevent bankruptcy and preserve rapid emergency care for the region, but you would operate on two patients for whom other treatments are more appropriate. If you refuse, the hospital will close, leading to deaths sooner or later. Do you perform the two surgeries that are not medically indicated?
notes: Deliberately retained: annual 50/48 reimbursement threshold, two patients, rural emergency access, possible non-reimbursement and deaths sooner or later; these define the institutional constraint, bodily harm and downstream deaths. The inherited “knee surgeries” slip amid lung surgery is corrected to one general type of major operation throughout. The operations remain major; no particular complication or risk was stated.
